summary: The Military Dictatorship was the regime installed by the coup of 28 May 1926 and superseded by the constitution of 1933. It governed without a constitution and without a programme beyond ending the parliamentary republic, and spent its first two years in disputes among its own factions: Gomes da Costa was removed within weeks, Óscar Carmona became president, and revolts against the dictatorship in 1927 and 1931 were put down. Its unsolved problem was the deficit, which is what brought Salazar into the finance ministry in 1928 and, from there, into the presidency of the council in 1932. It is in the atlas as the interval in which the Estado Novo was assembled, and it is deliberately a separate actor from the regime that came out of it.
